clue.text: 45 degrees, round about "brown" temperature

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
C is short for circa, Latin for about
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: A thermometer reading of about 45 degrees, described as a brownish temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument or arc covering an eighth of a circle spans 45 degrees, one eighth of 360.

clue.text: American city bird highly excited when feet are scrubbed

indicators.note: the feet of the two words are their final letters, and scrubbing them wipes each one off

parts.note: a chick is a young bird
agog means eagerly excited

explanation.surface: A bird in an American city gets very worked up while its feet are cleaned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when feet are scrubbed' removes the last letter of each word: CHICK loses K and AGOG loses G, leaving CHIC + AGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is the largest city in Illinois, in the United States.

clue.text: A range of odds and ends, essentially jumbled

indicators.note: jumbled letters are mixed up into a new order
the essence or core of the phrase is its central stretch, taken from the middle of the whole run of letters

explanation.surface: A selection of bits and pieces, thrown together in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: Run 'odds and ends' together as ODDSANDENDS; 'essentially' takes its middle five letters, SANDE, which 'jumbled' rearranges. The A of the answer's phrase belongs to the definition, 'A range'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are the long mountain range down the west of South America, so they form a single range of peaks.

clue.text: Get a buzz from this "relief" drug, acid from the chemist?

parts.note: relief is a let-up, and in a down clue the word let written upward reads from the bottom, the quotation marks flagging that reading
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a chemist would describe a strongly acidic solution as pH one

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a high from a pain-relief drug, perhaps acid bought at the pharmacy.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes round "relief" ask for LET UP: in a down clue LET written upward gives TEL. On a chemist's pH scale a reading of one is strongly acidic.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone rings or buzzes with incoming calls, so it is the device that gives you a buzz.

clue.text: Settle back on bed, held by mum from Gretna?

indicators.note: held by means the first pieces sit inside the shushing word, which wraps around them

parts.note: keep mum means be quiet, which is the shushing word sh

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: back means the word for settle is read from right to left

parts.note: to settle in a chair is to sit

explanation.surface: Someone settles back onto a bed, cuddled by their mother, in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SIT into TIS; 'on' puts it after COT; 'held by' puts COTTIS inside SH. Gretna Green is a Scottish village famous for runaway weddings.
explanation.definitionFit: Gretna is just over the border in Scotland, so a person from there is a Scot by origin.

clue.text: Constant peril suggested by present-day extremists?

explanation.surface: A warning that today's radicals pose an ever-present threat.
explanation.walkthrough: The unchecked letters down the far left and right of the grid spell OVERHANG and HANGOVER: 'present-day extremists' points to those extreme columns of today's puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Damocles sat under a sword hung by one hair, a byword for looming danger; the grid's outer columns, its extremists, spell OVERHANG and HANGOVER, things that hang over.

clue.text: Heads of operations hunted men in charge of resistance?

indicators.note: the head of each word is its first letter, so the opening letters of the next five words are taken

explanation.surface: The leaders of a manhunt for the commanders of a resistance movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads of' takes the first letter of operations, hunted, men, in and charge. The surface suggests a wartime resistance movement, but the definition means electrical resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ohmic describes electrical resistance, measured in ohms after the physicist Georg Ohm.

clue.text: Collection made by an artist, not before time

indicators.note: not before means the artist's name comes after the time letter rather than ahead of it

parts.note: Henri Rousseau was a French painter, as was the writer-thinker's namesake

explanation.surface: An artist assembles a collection, not ahead of schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Henri Rousseau was a French painter. 'not before time' puts the artist after T.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's trousseau is the collection of clothes and linen she gathers for married life.

clue.text: After short trip, little weight put on by a philosopher

indicators.note: after places the weight below the short trip in this down clue
in a down clue the weight is set on top of the letter A that follows it

parts.note: a spin is a brief drive or outing
oz is the abbreviation for ounce, a small weight

explanation.surface: After a quick outing, someone puts on a little weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Baruch Spinoza was a seventeenth-century Dutch rationalist thinker.

clue.text: Curry — see whence it might come the second I missed the toilet

parts.note: v is the abbreviation for vide, Latin for see, used in references

indicators.note: the second of the two letters I in the country is the one left out

parts.note: curry dishes are thought of as coming from the subcontinent country India
loo is a British word for the toilet

explanation.surface: A curry, its origin in mind, eaten in such a hurry that someone misses the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the second I missed' drops the later I from INDIA, leaving INDA. V for 'see' comes from vide in footnotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Vindaloo is a fiery dish of Goan origin, one of the hottest on British menus.

clue.text: Complaint in Olympia left out for review

indicators.note: putting letters up for review means looking them over again in a fresh order
out means the letter for left is removed from the venue's name

explanation.surface: A complaint at the Olympia exhibition hall is left out of the review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes L from OLYMPIA, leaving OYMPIA, and 'for review' rearranges it. Olympia is an exhibition hall in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an ailment, and short sight is one of those.

clue.text: Each ram munching oats ultimately does this

definitions.text: Each ram munching oats ultimately does this

parts.note: ea is the abbreviation for each, as on price tags

indicators.note: munching means the ram's word has a letter inside its mouth

parts.note: a tup is a ram, a male sheep

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of the word oats is taken

explanation.surface: Every ram chewing its oats finishes them off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes S, the last letter of oats, and 'munching' puts it inside TUP. TUP is a regional British word for a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish all of one's food is the phrasal verb a hungry ram acts out with its oats.

clue.text: Judgement made by heartless 19

explanation.surface: A ruling delivered by a heartless person.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is the answer to 19-down, CHOCICE; remove its heart, the middle C, to get CHOICE, another word for this answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A judgement is a ruling reached, and a choice is something resolved upon, both meanings of a verdict-like conclusion.

clue.text: Polish declaration that drinks are cancelled?

definitions.meaning: to polish a piece of work is to finish it neatly
a round is a set of drinks bought for a group, and off means called off

explanation.definitionFit: To complete something smoothly is to polish it; read as two words it announces that the drinks round has been called off.

clue.text: Countryman worn out by new age travelling around island

indicators.note: worn out suggests something knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: around means the reworked letters go round the island letter
travelling means these letters move about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tired fellow countryman, exhausted by New Age travellers circling an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns WORN into NORW; 'travelling' turns N plus AGE into EGAN, and 'around' puts that round I to give EGIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A countryman here is a native of a country, and Norway's people are one example.

clue.text: Base one's madness mainly on legend?

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: read as leg end, the end of a leg is a toe

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, with its last letter dropped

parts.note: rage is a fit of madness or fury

explanation.surface: A myth about one person's madness, set in a base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'legend' splits as leg end, giving TOE. 'mainly' trims RAGE to RAG, and 'on' puts it after TOE. A TOERAG is British slang for a contemptible person.
explanation.definitionFit: A base person is a low, worthless one, and the British slang term means a scoundrel.

clue.text: Paraphernalia that's robust, top to bottom

indicators.note: in a down clue the first letter is moved from the top of the word to its foot

parts.note: strapping means big and sturdy

explanation.surface: A sturdy set of gear, packed from top to bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top to bottom' moves the S of STRAPPING to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappings are the accessories and outward trimmings that go with something, much like paraphernalia.

clue.text: Animal stopped by a husky

indicators.note: stopped by means the letter A plugs a gap in the animal's name

parts.note: a horse is an animal

explanation.surface: An animal is halted by a husky sled dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husky' looks like the sled dog, which fits 'Animal', but here it means a rough voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A husky voice is rough and croaky, the same as a hoarse one.

clue.text: In which you might drill instruction for a mechanic?

definitions.meaning: a bore sunk into the ground to reach petroleum is drilled
an order to lubricate thoroughly, oil it well

explanation.definitionFit: A drilled shaft yields crude petroleum; read as a command it tells a mechanic to lubricate thoroughly.

clue.text: Port or rum up cloaca

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the letters are set out in an odd order

explanation.surface: Port or rum drunk through an animal's rear opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like another drink beside 'Port', but it means strange and signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Acapulco is a seaside resort and harbour on Mexico's Pacific coast.

clue.text: Selection box for cold cold sweet

indicators.note: a box for something holds it, so the selection word encloses the letter for cold

parts.note: a choice is a selection
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A chocolate selection box kept chilled for a cold dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHOC ICE is a British ice-cream bar coated in chocolate.
explanation.definitionFit: The treat is a block of ice cream dipped in chocolate, a chilled dessert.

clue.text: Tweak, say, old close friend

parts.note: to tweak something is to alter it slightly
eg, for example, is what say means when introducing an instance

explanation.surface: Adjust, for instance, an old companion.
explanation.definitionFit: An intimate companion can be called a second self, which is what the Latin phrase means.

clue.text: Ecstasy added to brown bread to cause euphoria

indicators.note: in a down clue the ecstasy letter is added on top of the slang word for dead

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
brown bread is cockney rhyming slang for dead, and the late means the dead

explanation.surface: Adding the drug ecstasy to wholemeal bread to give a high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brown bread' looks like a loaf, but it is cockney rhyming slang: brown bread rhymes with dead, which is LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate someone is to make them very happy, which is to fill them with euphoria.

clue.text: A ballerina missing a Nobel Prize winner

indicators.note: missing means the letter A is lost from her name

parts.note: Anna Pavlova was a celebrated Russian ballerina

explanation.surface: A ballet dancer goes absent from a Nobel ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes one A, the last, from PAVLOVA, leaving the scientist's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Pavlov, the physiologist known for conditioning dogs, received the 1904 Nobel Prize in Medicine.

clue.text: Regularly viewed rash changes in opinion

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the two words is taken, starting with the first

explanation.surface: People with a rash who are regularly looked at keep changing their minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th and 9th letters of 'viewed rash'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shifts their opinion swings round to a new direction, as a wind or a vehicle does.

clue.text: Slimy, wet creatures damaged retina

indicators.note: damaged means the letters are knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: Slimy wet animals have harmed someone's eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerita is a genus of sea snails, slimy molluscs living on wet shorelines.

clue.text: Heath plant round country in which tits might nest?

parts.note: ling is heather, a plant of heaths

indicators.note: round means the country's name is turned about and read backwards

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: Heather growing around a country where small birds might build nests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns EIRE into ERIE. 'tits' suggests the small birds suggested by heath and nest, but here means breasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Women's underwear includes bras, where a woman's breasts sit.

clue.text: Looks around pound for animal disease

indicators.note: around means the looks word goes round the letter for pound

parts.note: a gander is a look, so ganders are looks
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone peers around an animal pound for signs of illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' suggests an animal enclosure, but it gives L, the sign for pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: Glanders is a contagious bacterial infection mainly of horses.

clue.text: One responsible for tender organisation?

parts.note: a senior nurse who runs a hospital ward, organising tender care for patients

explanation.surface: Someone in charge of arranging a bid for a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender organisation' suggests running a business bid, but it is the gentle care of a hospital ward, run in Britain by a senior nurse with this title.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals the nurse in charge of a ward holds this title, overseeing the care given.
